title: SWP: how long does the money last?
objectives: Quote the illustrative SWP durations at 8% and label them correctly.
Explain why the withdrawal rate matters more than the fund, and why 1–2 years of withdrawals sit in a safe fund.
body_md:
A Systematic Withdrawal Plan redeems a fixed amount each month. The question every retiree asks is how long the money will last.

## The illustration

₹50 lakh at an assumed 8% a year, no inflation step-up, not a promise:

| Monthly withdrawal | Approximate duration |
|---|---|
| ₹30,000 | 20+ years (about ₹69.6 L still left after 20 years) |
| ₹40,000 | About 22 years |
| ₹45,000 | About 17 years |
| ₹50,000 | About 14 years |

The withdrawal rate matters far more than which fund is chosen. A small change in the monthly amount moves the end date by years.

## The buffer

Keep 1–2 years of withdrawals in a liquid or short-duration fund, so a market fall never forces equity sales at low prices. In a long fall, the buffer pays the client while the equity portion recovers.

## How to say it

"Illustratively, at 8% assumed, ₹40,000 a month could last about 22 years — not guaranteed." Never say the money *will* last a stated number of years.
example: Mr. Iyer has ₹50 lakh and needs ₹45,000 a month. The illustration shows about 17 years at 8%, so the conversation turns to a lower withdrawal, his pension income, and a one-year buffer in a liquid fund.
say: At 8% assumed, ₹45,000 a month could last about 17 years; that is an illustration, not a promise.
Let's keep one to two years of withdrawals in a liquid fund so a fall doesn't force us to sell equity.
never: The SWP is guaranteed for life.

talk_track.title: SWP: how long does ₹50 lakh last?
talk_track.text: How long does fifty lakh last? At an assumed eight percent a year: withdrawing thirty thousand a month, it lasts well over twenty years, with about seventy lakh still left after twenty years. Forty thousand a month lasts about twenty-two years. Forty-five thousand, about seventeen. Fifty thousand, about fourteen. The withdrawal rate matters far more than which fund is chosen. And keep one to two years of withdrawals in a liquid or short-duration fund, so a market fall never forces equity sales at low prices.

o: Redeems a fixed amount at regular intervals
check.why: A Systematic Withdrawal Plan redeems a fixed amount at regular intervals, which is how a retiree takes income.

check.q: ₹50 lakh at an assumed 8%: roughly how long does ₹45,000 a month last?
check.why: About 17 years in the illustration. It is not a promise.

check.q: Why keep 1–2 years of withdrawals in a liquid fund?
o: So a market fall does not force equity sales at low prices
check.why: The buffer pays the client through a fall so the equity portion is not sold at the bottom.
